        <dc:title>TRANSIMS traffic flow characteristics</dc:title>
            <dc:creator>Nagel, Kai</dc:creator>
            <dc:creator>Stretz, Paula</dc:creator>
            <dc:creator>Pieck, Martin</dc:creator>
            <dc:creator>Donnelly, Rick</dc:creator>
            <dc:creator>Barrett, Christopher L.</dc:creator>
            <dc:subject>Adaptation and Self-Organizing Systems</dc:subject>
            <dc:description>  Knowledge of fundamental traffic flow characteristics of traffic simulation models is an essential requirement when using these models for the planning, design, and operation of transportation systems. In this paper we discuss the following: a description of how features relevant to traffic flow are currently under implementation in the TRANSIMS microsimulation, a proposition for standardized traffic flow tests for traffic simulation models, and the results of these tests for two different versions of the TRANSIMS microsimulation. </dc:description>
            <dc:description>Paper has 23 pages, 5 figures, 28 diagrams</dc:description>
